entries.topicDescription: Understanding app states, scene delegates, and background execution.

tips.title: ScenePhase tracks your app's foreground state
tips.content:
In SwiftUI, the @Environment(\.scenePhase) property tells
you whether your app is active, inactive, or in the
background. This replaces UIApplicationDelegate callbacks.

Active means the app is in the foreground and receiving
events. Inactive is a transient state (e.g., during a
phone call overlay). Background means the app is not visible.

Use .onChange(of: scenePhase) to react to transitions: save
data when going to background, refresh content when becoming
active, or pause timers when inactive.

For multi-window iPad apps, each window has its own scene
phase. The app-level phase is the aggregate of all scenes.

tips.title: Background tasks with BGTaskScheduler
tips.content:
iOS suspends your app shortly after it enters the background.
For deferred work (data sync, cleanup), register a background
task with BGTaskScheduler.

There are two types: BGAppRefreshTask for short periodic
updates (30 seconds), and BGProcessingTask for longer work
(minutes) when the device is charging and idle.

Register task identifiers in Info.plist under
BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers. Schedule tasks before
your app goes to background.

Always call task.setTaskCompleted(success:) when done.
Handle the task's expirationHandler to clean up if the
system is reclaiming resources.

tips.title: Deep links and universal links route users to content
tips.content:
Deep links let other apps or websites open specific screens
in your app. iOS supports two kinds: custom URL schemes
(myapp://profile/42) and universal links (https://myapp.com/profile/42).

Universal links are preferred because they're secure (Apple
verifies domain ownership via apple-app-site-association),
and they fall back to Safari if the app isn't installed.

In SwiftUI, handle incoming URLs with .onOpenURL. Parse the
URL components and navigate to the appropriate screen. Use
an enum-based routing system to keep navigation logic clean.

Test deep links from Terminal with 'xcrun simctl openurl'
during development. Remember to handle both cold launches
and warm opens.
